label: Isaac Newton, Philosophiae naturalis…: Newton's first law, conditional content: a body changes its…
locator: Axiomata, Lex I: Corpus omne perseverare in statu suo quiescendi vel movendi uniformiter in directum, nisi quatenus a viribus impressis cogitur statum illum mutare
interpretation: Every body perseveres in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line, except insofar as impressed forces compel it to change that state; projectiles persevere in their motions except as air resistance and gravity act on them. Read as its conditional content: a body changes its state only if some force is impressed on it. Newton calls uniform motion a state (status) and asserts no existence of a body free of forces; his examples are bodies acted on by resistance and gravity. The inertial rival STMT-INERTIAL-UNIFORM-MOTION-WITHOUT-MOVER, which adds a force-free moving body and reads uniform motion as a being moved, is not attributed to this sentence.
